citations.B1: Check-then-act race: `get` and the assignment are separate operations, so N threads can all read `count = 99` and all pass
citations.B2: Lost updates on the write itself: concurrent `counts[user_id] = count + 1` overwrite each other, so the stored count drifts below the true number of admitted requests
citations.B3: fix by doing the read-increment under a single `threading.Lock`
citations.B4: It is not a rate limiter: counts never reset, so it is a lifetime quota
citations.B5: Unbounded memory growth: one permanent entry per distinct `user_id`
citations.B6: an in-process dict is per-worker, so with W workers the effective limit is `limit × W`
citations.B7: `user_id` is unvalidated: `None` or an empty value collapses all anonymous callers into one bucket
